_comment: V2 Phase 1B (BL-021, docs/v2/10-BACKLOG.md). Built only from the 10 trait entities that actually exist in live data/entities/traits/ (2026-08-14) -- not an exhaustive horticultural ontology, per this task's own instruction. ids and descriptions are copied verbatim from the live entities for traceability; measurement_type/unit are derived directly from each description's own wording (e.g. 'reported in degrees Brix' -> unit: degrees Brix), not invented. This is the same trait id list entity-types.json's variety entry references.

traits.label: Chilling requirement
traits.description: Accumulated hours below a stated threshold temperature needed to break dormancy. Thresholds differ between sources (7 °C is common in Florida literature).
traits.unit: hours below threshold temperature (threshold itself varies by source)

traits.label: Disease susceptibility
traits.description: Reported susceptibility or tolerance to specific pathogens.

traits.label: Eating quality
traits.description: Sweetness, acidity, Brix, Brix/acid ratio and sensory panel scores. UF/IFAS publishes a numeric flavour score; the International Taste Institute issues independent star awards.
traits._comment: Composite: numeric flavor score, star-award scale, or sensory panel, depending on source -- not one consistent unit.

traits.label: Fruit firmness
traits.description: Resistance of the berry to compression. Measured differently by different programmes: UF/IFAS publishes a g/mm compression index; US plant patents sometimes cite FirmTech instrument readings; PBR examination reports use ordinal descriptors. Values from different methods are not directly comparable.
traits._comment: The source description itself warns values across methods are not directly comparable -- deliberately not normalized to one unit here.

traits.label: Fruit size
traits.description: Berry weight (g) and/or equatorial diameter (mm). Marketing terms such as 'jumbo' are owner claims, not measurements.

traits.label: Machine-harvest suitability
traits.description: Whether a cultivar can be mechanically harvested for the fresh market without unacceptable quality loss.

traits.label: Post-harvest shelf life
traits.description: Number of days of acceptable quality in cold storage. Almost always an owner or marketer claim; storage temperature, packaging and quality threshold are usually unstated.

traits.label: Soluble solids content
traits.description: Sugar concentration of the fruit, normally reported in degrees Brix. Recorded as a separate trait because Brix figures are published by owners, by independent trials and by registries using different sampling points in the season, and are frequently quoted without a method.

traits.label: Titratable acidity
traits.description: Measured acid content of the fruit, reported as a percentage. Together with soluble solids it determines perceived sweetness, and it is rarely published outside independent trials.

traits.label: Yield
traits.description: Harvested fruit per plant or per hectare, normally reported with a location and season.
traits.unit: fruit per plant or per hectare

traits.label: Fruiting habit
traits.description: Whether a caneberry cultivar fruits on first-year canes (primocane, fall-fruiting) or second-year canes (floricane, summer-fruiting), or both. Added for the multi-berry portability audit (2026-08-20) -- the original 10 traits above were all derived from the blueberry-only pilot and had no entry for this categorical growth-habit distinction, which is the primary variety-differentiator for raspberry and blackberry breeding.

traits.label: Flowering habit
traits.description: Whether a strawberry cultivar flowers in response to short daylength (short-day / June-bearing) or largely independent of daylength (day-neutral / everbearing). Added for the multi-berry portability audit (2026-08-20), same reason as trait-fruiting-habit.

traits.label: Fruit color
traits.description: Reported fruit color or color intensity of a variety. Added for the Raspberry Vertical V1 depth mission (2026-08-20) -- a real, generic gap found while adding Cornell's raspberry release Crimson Treasure, whose own coverage described 'vibrant colors' as a stated selling point with no existing trait entity to record it against. Applicable across all four berries, not raspberry-specific.

unresolved_overlap_candidates.note: eating-quality's own description explicitly names 'Brix' and 'Brix/acid ratio' -- the same underlying measurements soluble-solids (Brix) and titratable-acidity (acid %) each already record separately, and more precisely, as their entire purpose. eating-quality appears to be a composite/subjective umbrella that partially restates the other two rather than a fully independent trait. Kept as three separate entries (matching live data, which already keeps them separate) rather than merged here -- a modeling decision for a human, not resolved by this task.
